chapter: Idaho tours, Music Town and retirement
title: Music Town: songwriting service and dance hall, 1941-45
summary: With Austin McCoy, Spikes ran a song-for-hire business, recorded demos, rented a dance hall to bands like Les Hite and Benny Carter, then went into real estate until 1962.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: music for Noble Sissle when he came to town and the Duncan Sisters when they were showing out in Hollywood, and, oh, we opened up a business of doing music for people all over the United States. We carried big ads in the papers, and we got sometimes do ten, twelve, fifteen songs a week. They send in the word...the words, we put music to it; they send the music, we put words to it, or they had an idea, we'd...just a bunch of words--we'd make a song out of it and make a record and send it to them, you know, and we had our own little machine that you cut your own little records, and we'd send them a record of the song, and we'd get ten or twelve dollars for it, and we's doing twenty, thirty of them a week, and doing the ads, you know. And besides that, we had...we rented the hall for dancing up there. We had two, three dances a week, and during the day, we had band rehearsals--Les Hite, Benny Carter, and a lot of other bands used to come up there and rehearse, and then we had all of the other activities like dancing classes and drama classes and such as that, and we had several teachers that was doing that, so we got along pretty good till uh...after we were around...uh, let's see, I don't know what year it was. I think it was '41 or '42, Austin McCoy, who I had up there with me in partners was drafted, and he went to [Fort] Huachuca, Arizona, to the Twenty-Fourth Infantry down there, I think, and when the war was over, they let him come back, and that was about '45, and we stayed there about three years, and we dissolved partnerships, and he went on his own and opened up his own recording studio in Watts, and I went in the real estate business, and I stayed in the real estate business until '62, I think. That was about ten
or twelve years, and then I retired.
